> Without using any tools, explain how a coding agent like you works, for a new teammate. Use a 
short heading and a few bullet points.
How a coding agent like me works                                                                    

 • The loop: You give me a task in plain language. I decide what I need to know, call a tool, read  
   the result, and repeat until the task is done. Then I summarize what I did.                      
 • My tools: I can search (Glob for file names, Grep for contents), read files (Read), change files 
   (Edit for small changes, Write for new files or full rewrites), and run shell commands (Bash)    
   such as tests, git, and package installs.                                                        
 • Look before changing: I read a file before I edit it. Edits are exact find-and-replace, so I need
   the file's real contents rather than a guess.                                                    
 • Parallel work: When several lookups don't depend on each other, such as reading three files, I   
   run them together. When one result decides the next step, I wait for it.                         
 • Small changes: I aim for the smallest change that solves the task. I try not to refactor or      
   reformat code you didn't ask me to touch.                                                        
 • Verification: After a change, I run the tests or the relevant command when I can. That way I     
   report what actually happened, not what I expect to happen.                                      
 • Limits: I only know what's in the conversation and what my tools show me. I can be wrong, misread
   unfamiliar code, or miss context that lives in your heads. Review my diffs the way you'd review a
   teammate's, and tell me if I've misunderstood the goal.                                          
 • Working with me: Specific requests work best. Say which file, which behavior, and what "done"    
   looks like. If the request is ambiguous, I may ask or state my assumption.

## How a coding agent like me works

- **Loop of think, act, observe:** I read your request and decide what I need to know. Then I call a tool, look at the result, and repeat until the task is done. After that I summarize what I did.
- **Tools are my hands:** I can search (Glob for filenames, Grep for contents), read files (Read), change them (Edit for small changes, Write for new files or full rewrites), and run shell commands (Bash) for tests, git and installs. I only see and change the project through these tools.
- **Read before editing:** I always look at a file before changing it. Edits are exact find-and-replace, so I need the real text. This also helps me match the existing style and avoid breaking things.
- **Parallel when possible:** If several lookups don't depend on each other, such as reading three files, I run them together to save time. If one step needs another's output, I wait for it.
- **Small, focused changes:** I try to make the smallest change that solves the task. I avoid unrelated refactors, and I run tests when they're available to check my work.
- **Limits to know about:** I only know what's in my context: your messages, the files I've read, and command output. I can be wrong, so review my diffs, especially for anything risky. Clear requests with a goal, relevant files, and how to verify the result get the best results.
- **Working with me:** Treat me like a quick junior pair-programmer. Give me context, let me explore the code, and check the result before you merge it.
